system:
You compress serialized-story history for writers who must stay consistent later.
Keep: who did what, what changed, secrets learned and by whom, deaths/injuries/locations, unresolved questions,
promises and threats made. Drop: prose, mood, anything that didn't change the story. Plain factual sentences.
user:
Merge into one 'story so far' of <=700 words:
Arc 1: A body was found wearing Aadit’s coat and an apparent ring. Meher recognized the coat and ring in a photograph but not the face, so Bhuvan kept the identification provisional and prevented Raghav from claiming the body before examination. He later confirmed the dead man was not Aadit, though the body remained unidentified.

At 6:12, a man sounding like Aadit called Meher from a borrowed phone, refused to speak to police, and said he expected her to be suspected. Bus driver Jitendra Rawat confirmed that a man borrowed his phone and asked to call Meher by name. He found a dark-red-spotted handkerchief where the man sat at Anardana Dhaba; Bhuvan collected it and found a grocery slip bearing Meher’s name beneath the bench. Jitendra said the caller stayed outside the dhaba when his 6:20 bus left and did not board. Naina corrected her initial message to Bhuvan, which had named Aadit.

Meher’s account of the previous night was uncertain. Shanta said Meher’s room was empty at 9:40, contradicting Meher’s claim she stayed there until 10:00; Bhuvan struck that claim from her timeline.

Aadit returned to Cedar Terrace and admitted borrowing Jitendra’s phone. He said he left the shed on the night of the fire and stayed in the orchard pump room, but would not identify the person he went to meet. Meher demanded he explain himself to Bhuvan. Asked how his coat and ring reached the body, Aadit said he had left his wedding ring in a blue biscuit tin before going to the shed.

Meher hid a novel she wrote under a pen name; its plot resembles her husband’s apparent death. Tara told Meher she had been told her baby died eight years earlier and recalled Manu’s care and his theft from her till.
